original_question: In the localized phase, let μ(λ,h) := -lim_{N→∞} (1/N) log E[(1 + exp(-2λ Σ_{n=1}^N (ω_n+h)))/Z_{N,ω}] and let F(λ,h) be the free energy. As h approaches the critical curve h_c(λ) from below, are the two quantities logarithmically equivalent in the sense that log μ(λ,h) ~ log F(λ,h)? This asks whether the decay scale controlling correlation length or longest-excursion asymptotics vanishes at the same logarithmic rate as the free energy near criticality.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1, read together with Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3: the paper asks whether the annealed decay rate μ(λ,h) and the quenched free energy F(λ,h) have the same logarithmic critical behavior as h approaches h_c(λ) from the localized side.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right open problem: it uses the correct quantity μ(λ,h), compares it to the free energy F(λ,h) as h approaches the critical curve from below, and correctly identifies the intended interpretation in terms of the decay scale for correlations / longest excursions in the localized phase. It is also appropriately narrower than neighboring questions about exact critical exponents or the full phase diagram.
missing_details: State explicitly that λ is fixed and positive, and that the limit is taken with h increasing to h_c(λ) from the localized region h<h_c(λ).
Specify the ambient model: the standard disordered copolymer near a selective interface treated in the paper, not the more general copolymer-with-adsorption model from earlier work.
Define the quenched free energy in the paper’s normalization, namely F(λ,h)=lim_{N→∞}(1/N)log Z_{N,ω}^{λ,h} almost surely (or equivalently in expectation, if using the paper’s stated convention).
Define the critical line h_c(λ):=sup{h: F(λ,h)>0} (equivalently the boundary between localized and delocalized phases).
Specify that Z_{N,ω}^{λ,h} is the partition function of the copolymer model used in the paper; otherwise μ(λ,h) is not fully stand-alone.
State the exact asymptotic notion meant by “logarithmically equivalent”: lim_{h↑h_c(λ)} log μ(λ,h) / log F(λ,h) = 1.

Mention the paper’s proven comparison bounds from Theorem 1.3, which motivate the conjecture: 0 ≤ μ(λ,h) ≤ F(λ,h), together with a quadratic lower bound of the form c F(λ,h)^2 ≤ μ(λ,h) under the stated parameter restrictions.

If you want the ‘correlation length’ interpretation to be fully explicit, name which length scale is meant: the inverse exponential decay rate associated via Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 to the averaged correlation decay or, equivalently in the paper’s discussion, to the longest-excursion scale 1/μ(λ,h).
The disorder assumptions are implicit in your draft; to be fully paper-faithful, they should be taken exactly as in the paper’s copolymer model setup rather than left unspecified.
refined_question:
For the standard disordered copolymer near a selective interface considered in arXiv:1010.5587, fix λ>0, let F(λ,h)=lim_{N→∞}(1/N)log Z_{N,ω}^{λ,h} be the quenched free energy, and let h_c(λ)=sup{h:F(λ,h)>0} be the critical curve. In the localized phase h<h_c(λ), define
μ(λ,h):=-lim_{N→∞}(1/N)log E[(1+exp(-2λ∑_{n=1}^N(ω_n+h)))/Z_{N,ω}^{λ,h}],
so that Theorem 1.3 identifies 1/μ(λ,h) as the scale governing longest-excursion asymptotics and gives 0≤μ(λ,h)≤F(λ,h) (with a quadratic lower bound). Is it true that, for every fixed λ>0,
lim_{h↑h_c(λ)} (log μ(λ,h))/(log F(λ,h)) = 1?
In other words, does the length scale controlled by μ(λ,h) diverge, up to logarithmic equivalence, at the same rate as 1/F(λ,h) when the critical curve is approached from the localized side?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation from Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3: for fixed λ>0, is the disorder-averaged correlation-length scale (equivalently, the longest-excursion scale 1/μ(λ,h)) logarithmically equivalent to 1/F(λ,h) as h↑h_c(λ)?
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper’s main open problem in the introductory part, not at a broader neighboring question. Conjecture 1.1 asks for the critical comparison between μ(λ,h) and F(λ,h) near h_c(λ). Proposition 1.2 supplies the reformulation in terms of the relevant correlation-length scale, and Theorem 1.3 supplies the precise role of μ(λ,h) through longest-excursion asymptotics together with the bounds 0≤μ≤F and μ≳F^2 that make the conjecture meaningful. Your draft already matches that target closely; the main improvements needed are to make the model, quantifiers, normalization of F, definition of h_c(λ), and the exact logarithmic-limit statement fully explicit and self-contained.
